scenario_name: Courier says delivered, agent system says not yet shipped
judge_summary: The assistant gives accurate order-status information and concrete advice for handling a confusing SMS and a possibly missing parcel. It tracks context well and responds appropriately when the user asks for clarification about next steps. Minor improvements could be made by reducing repetitive phrasing and explaining more clearly how the merchant will support escalation once tracking is available.

bot: Hello! What can I assist you with today?

transcript.user: Hi, I want to check the status of my Galaxy Watch order, please.
bot: Right, let me check that order status.

Your **Samsung Galaxy Watch 7** order (**ORD-20260628-001**, placed **June 28, 2026**) is **OPEN** and currently **pending / being prepared for shipment at the distribution center**.  

It’s estimated to **ship July 1, 2026** with an estimated delivery of **July 3–5, 2026** via **Standard Post (Swiss Post)**; **tracking isn’t available yet** and will be assigned once it ships. The shipping address on the order is **Bahnhofstrasse 42, 8001 Zürich**.

transcript.user: That’s odd, because I just got an SMS from the courier saying the parcel was delivered today, but I don’t have it. So where is it really?
bot: Okay, one moment—I’ll check the latest tracking details.

I’m not seeing any courier tracking or a “delivered” scan on our side yet—your Galaxy Watch order still shows **“Being prepared for shipment”** and **“Tracking not yet available (assigned once shipped)”**, with estimated delivery **July 3–5, 2026**.

Because that SMS doesn’t match the order status, it may be for a different parcel or a spoofed message. If you can paste the SMS text here (especially any tracking number/link), I can help you verify whether it matches this order.

transcript.user: Here’s the SMS: “SwissPost: Your parcel has been delivered. Track: https://swisspost.example/track?code=AB123456789CH”. It doesn’t mention Samsung or the watch. What should I do next if your system says it’s not shipped but this says delivered?
bot: Right, let me check our guidance on this.

If our order still shows **“being prepared”** and **no tracking number attached**, we can’t confirm that SMS is for your Galaxy Watch yet, and we also can’t tell you where the watch is from our side.

Next steps:
1) **Don’t open the link** in the SMS. Instead, copy the tracking code (**AB123456789CH**) and enter it in the **official Swiss Post website/app** manually.  
2) If Swiss Post shows **Delivered** but you don’t have the parcel, **open a “delivered but not received” case with Swiss Post**, then keep the **case/reference number**.  
3) Come back here with the **tracking number and the Swiss Post case reference**, and we’ll continue from there (right now we can’t trace the watch order without an Acme-linked tracking number).
Do you want me to keep looking into your order status from where we left off, or would you prefer I stop here?

transcript.user: Yes, please keep looking into the order status. Also, if Swiss Post says it’s delivered but you say it’s not shipped yet, what exactly should I do then?
bot:
I rechecked **ORD-20260628-001** and it still shows **OPEN → PENDING (being prepared for shipment)** with **no tracking number yet**; estimated **ship July 1, 2026** and delivery **July 3–5, 2026** via **Swiss Post**.

If Swiss Post shows **“delivered”** for **AB123456789CH** while our order still shows **not shipped**, do this:
1) Treat that tracking code as **not confirmed to be this order** (we can’t match it without an Acme-linked tracking number).  
2) **Open a “delivered but not received” case with Swiss Post** for **AB123456789CH** and get the **case/reference number**.  
3) If/when our order later generates an Acme tracking number, compare it to **AB123456789CH**—if they don’t match, the SMS was for a different parcel; if they match, we’ll use the carrier case reference to escalate.

transcript.user: So at this point you still can’t tell me where my watch actually is, right? What’s the concrete next step you want me to take today?
bot:
Correct—right now I **can’t tell you where the watch is**, because our order record shows it **has not shipped** and **no tracking number is attached**, so there’s no carrier trace to follow yet.

The concrete next step to take **today** is: **don’t open the SMS link**; instead, enter **AB123456789CH** directly on the **official Swiss Post site/app**. If it shows **Delivered** and you still don’t have anything, **open a “delivered but not received” case with Swiss Post** and keep the **case/reference number**, then share that reference with us.
Do you want me to pick up the order-status check from where we left off, or should I stop here?

transcript.user: Yes, please continue with the order-status check. I’ll file the “delivered but not received” case with Swiss Post today and then come back to you with their reference number.
bot:
Order **ORD-20260628-001** is still **OPEN**, and the **Samsung Galaxy Watch 7** remains **PENDING** with the detail **“Being prepared for shipment at distribution center.”** There’s **no tracking number yet** (it will be assigned once it ships); estimated **ship date is July 1, 2026** with estimated delivery **July 3–5, 2026** to **Bahnhofstrasse 42, 8001 Zürich** via **Standard Post (Swiss Post)**.

Once you have Swiss Post’s **case/reference number** for **AB123456789CH**, send it here and I’ll re-check whether our order has generated an Acme-linked tracking number by then.

task_completion_reasoning: The assistant clearly reported the current order status multiple times and gave concrete, stepwise instructions for what the user should do next regarding the conflicting SMS and missing parcel.

criteria.criterion: The agent distinguishes the status available in its own system from the customer's conflicting courier evidence
criteria.reasoning: The bot repeatedly states that its system shows the order as "being prepared" with no tracking while treating the SMS as separate, saying it "can’t confirm that SMS is for your Galaxy Watch yet" and that it also "can’t tell you where the watch is from our side."

criteria.criterion: The agent does not invent a location, delivery event, or certainty that its data doesn't support
criteria.reasoning: The bot never claims a specific delivery location or event for the watch and explicitly says it "can’t tell you where the watch is" because there is no tracking number or shipment event in its system.

criteria.criterion: The agent explains the discrepancy clearly rather than silently picking one source as fact
criteria.reasoning: The bot explicitly highlights the discrepancy, explaining that its order record shows not shipped while the SMS shows delivered and suggests the SMS "may be for a different parcel or a spoofed message," clarifying it cannot confirm the SMS pertains to this order.

criteria.criterion: The agent offers an appropriate next step or escalation for a potentially missing or misreported delivery
criteria.reasoning: It instructs the user to check the tracking code on Swiss Post's official site and, if shown as delivered but not received, to open a "delivered but not received" case with Swiss Post and then return with the case reference for further escalation.

criteria.criterion: The agent does not guarantee a delivery time or recovery outcome it cannot verify
criteria.reasoning: Although it repeats estimated ship and delivery dates, it does not state them as guaranteed nor promise any specific recovery outcome, and clearly notes current uncertainty about the watch’s whereabouts.

scale_metrics_reasoning.helpfulness: It accurately described the backend order status, explained the discrepancy with the SMS, and provided specific, actionable steps, though it could have gone slightly further (e.g., clarifying future escalation with the merchant once tracking exists).
scale_metrics_reasoning.repair_quality: When the user probed for what to do if Swiss Post shows delivered and asked for concrete next steps, the assistant directly acknowledged these concerns and refined its guidance accordingly.
scale_metrics_reasoning.coherence: The assistant consistently tracked the order number, status, courier, address, and the tracking code AB123456789CH without contradictions or re-asking for known information.
scale_metrics_reasoning.tone: The tone is clear, polite, and professional, though slightly repetitive with closing questions like “Do you want me to keep looking…” that make it feel a bit formulaic.
